Generate a random key

Source: R/keys.R
jwk_generate.Rd

jwk_generate() makes a new key from the operating system's cryptographic random source, through zucrypt: oct, RSA, EC (on P-256, P-384 or P-521) and OKP (X25519) keys. There is no Ed25519.

Usage

jwk_generate(
  kty,
  size = NULL,
  crv = NULL,
  alg = NULL,
  kid = NULL,
  use = NULL,
  key_ops = NULL
)

Arguments

kty

The key type: "oct", "RSA", "EC" or "OKP".

size

The key size in bits. For an oct key, a multiple of 8 and at least 128, and NULL takes the size alg needs; for an RSA key, 2048 to 4096, and NULL is 2048.

crv

The curve: "P-256" (the default), "P-384" or "P-521" for an EC key, "X25519" for an OKP key. Not used otherwise.

alg

The one algorithm the key is meant for, such as "HS256", or NULL. When set, a token whose alg differs is refused.

kid

A key identifier, or NULL. See jwk_with_kid().

use

"sig" or "enc", or NULL.

key_ops

The operations the key may be used for, from "sign", "verify", "encrypt", "decrypt", "wrapKey", "unwrapKey", "deriveKey" and "deriveBits", or NULL.

Value

A jwk.

Details

Without size, an oct key is as long as alg needs: the hash size for HS256, HS384 and HS512 (RFC 7518 section 3.2), the key size for A*KW and A*GCMKW, and 256 bits otherwise. A dir key is the content encryption key itself, so give its size: 256 bits for A128CBC-HS256, 384 for A192CBC-HS384, 512 for A256CBC-HS512, and 128, 192 or 256 for A128GCM, A192GCM and A256GCM.

An RSA key's size is its modulus, 2048 bits by default and at most 4096, with public exponent 65537. Generating one takes a moment.

Secrets in memory

zujose is pure R, and so are its keys: an oct secret, and the private members of an RSA, EC or X25519 key, are ordinary R vectors. R copies vectors freely and has no way to wipe one, so a secret may stay in memory after the key is gone, and may reach a saved workspace or a core dump. zujose never prints secret members and never puts them in an error message, but it cannot do more than that. Keep long-lived secrets out of saved workspaces (.RData) and load them from a secret store when they are needed.

See also

jwk_oct() to wrap a secret you already have, jwk_with_kid() to name the new key by its thumbprint.

Examples

key <- jwk_generate("oct", alg = "HS256")
key
#> <jwk> oct, 256 bits
#>   alg HS256
#>   private: yes (not shown)

# A key encryption key, named by its thumbprint.
jwk_with_kid(jwk_generate("oct", alg = "A256KW"))
#> <jwk> oct, 256 bits
#>   kid "CMrU3pzG7XZ_mY0R2MRytRRYNHra0tbhKAzT3aw3hWM"
#>   alg A256KW
#>   private: yes (not shown)
